claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch as compliant based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public risk-management/model-card guidance despite an unresolved shelter-segment performance gap tied to a named launch use case and open legal review.
decision_criteria: A compliant verdict requires admissible evidence that the certification satisfies the internal policy for material weaknesses affecting named launch use cases.
If the limitation was disclosed as required before launch, or an approved risk acceptance exists, the verdict could improve.
If primary evidence shows the use case is not actually a named launch use case or customer commitment, the materiality concern could weaken.
Absent those predicates, aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents are insufficient to establish compliance.
evidence_requests: The underlying release policy text and any implementing procedures governing disclosure and pre-launch risk acceptance.
The actual legal review status, including whether counsel concluded disclosure is required.
Any approved risk-acceptance record covering the shelter-segment gap before launch.
The model card or disclosure artifact that would inform customers or stakeholders of the shelter-segment limitation.
Primary evidence for the two nonprofit deployment commitments naming the affected use case.
Primary evaluation results showing the 1.5 percentage point miss and the aggregate 2.1 point pass.
specific_concerns: The cited support appears to show operational readiness in aggregate, but not satisfaction of the policy predicate for a named launch use case with an unresolved gap.
The available policy text says materiality is triggered when a weakness affects a named launch use case, and product-label arguments do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
The Actor's own summary preserves contrary facts: the shelter segment misses target, is named in deployment commitments, and legal review remains open.

Public NIST and model-card guidance can support monitoring and documentation practices, but they do not by themselves authorize certification where an internal disclosure or risk-acceptance condition may be unmet.
No admissible evidence is provided showing the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance, which the packet itself identifies as the relevant policy condition.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That public governance guidance is sufficient to overcome or satisfy the internal materiality/disclosure requirement.
Any implicit claim that the shelter-segment gap is non-material despite its connection to a named launch use case and pending legal review.
